# An unsealed local edit made BEFORE the merge starts, to a secret the merge
# then replaces. The finalize used to pick a side on its own - first the merge's
# (overwriting the edit), later the user's (dropping theirs). Now it refuses,
# and taking the merge's version is an explicit step.

sesam-repo admin base.txt ours.txt changed.txt local.txt

cp $TMPDIR/base.txt s
cp $TMPDIR/base.txt t
exec sesam add s --group admin
exec sesam add t --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add secrets'

exec git checkout -b topic
cp $TMPDIR/changed.txt t
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'topic: change t'

exec git checkout master
cp $TMPDIR/ours.txt s
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'master: change s'

# The unsealed edit, then the merge.
cp $TMPDIR/local.txt t
! exec git merge topic
exec cat t
stdout 'LOCAL-UNSEALED'

! exec git commit --no-edit
stderr 'changed both here and in this merge'
stderr '  t'

exec sesam reveal --all
exec git commit --no-edit
exec sesam show .sesam/objects/t.sesam
stdout 'CHANGED'
exec cat t
stdout 'CHANGED'
exec sesam verify
stderr 'Integrity: ok'

-- base.txt --
BASE
-- ours.txt --
OURS
-- changed.txt --
CHANGED
-- local.txt --
LOCAL-UNSEALED
